verses.40:2: Bem-aventurado o que {intellegit}: * no dia mau o livrará o Senhor.
verses.40:3: O Senhor o conserve, e {vivificet}, e o faça bem-aventurado na terra: * e não o entregue {inanimam} dos seus inimigos.
verses.40:4: O Senhor lhe traga {opem} {superlectum} da sua dor: * toda a sua cama {versasti} na sua enfermidade.
verses.40:5: Eu disse: Senhor, tende piedade de mim: * curai a minha alma, porque pequei contra vós.
verses.40:6: Os meus inimigos disseram {mihi6}: * Quando morrerá, e perecerá o seu nome?
verses.40:7: E, se entrava para {videret}, falava coisas vãs: * o seu coração juntou iniquidade para si.
verses.40:8: Contra mim {susurrabant} todos os meus inimigos: * contra mim pensavam em {mihi8}.
verses.40:9: Estabeleceram contra mim uma palavra iníqua: * Acaso o que dorme não tornará a {resurgat}?
verses.40:10: {etenim} o homem da minha paz, em quem esperei: * que comia {panes}, {supplantatio}.
verses.40:11: Vós, porém, Senhor, tende piedade de mim, e {resuscita}: * e eu lhes retribuirei.
verses.40:12: Nisto conheci que {voluisti}: * porque o meu inimigo não se alegrará à minha custa.
verses.40:13: Mas a mim, por causa {innocentia}, amparastes: * e me firmastes {conspectu} para sempre.
verses.40:14: Bendito o Senhor, Deus de Israel, {asaeculo}: * {fiat}.

decisions.latin: qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem
decisions.why: intellégere → entender (glossary, working); *super* (ἐπί) makes it 'understand concerning', i.e. give thought to the poor man's case (DRB 'understandeth concerning'). *entender sobre* is not Portuguese; *entender alguém* is, and means to grasp his situation. MS1932 *cuida do* says the act of care, which the Latin does not name. The verse is an Alleluia verse and a Gradual (Pent01-0a, missa Sancti/04-28, 07-18 — grep), so it will be heard alone. v2: the Latinist (minor) marked *super* dropped, and the stylist and the blind reader both heard *entende o necessitado* as psychological sympathy. *super* is restored as *acerca de*, which also makes the verb one of taking thought.

forms.intellegit: entende acerca do necessitado e do pobre

options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latinist's fix — the glossary verb and the preposition both kept; DRB 'understandeth concerning'. Long (+5 on the Latin colon), accepted.

forms.intellegit: atende ao necessitado e ao pobre

options.label: o que cuida do necessitado e do pobre

forms.intellegit: cuida do necessitado e do pobre

options.note: MS1932; says what the Latin does not (care).

decisions.why: vivificáre → vivificar is the glossary's working word (row open; Ps 118 has it twelve times). A blind reader of Ps 118 listed it as unknown. 40:3 is the versicle said for the Pope in the Preces (Preces.txt — grep), so the three verbs *conserve … vivifique … faça bem-aventurado* will be said alone.

options.label: o vivifique
options.note: Ruling: one word for one, as in Ps 118.

options.label: lhe dê vida
options.note: MS1932, DRB 'give him life'; the row's option.

decisions.why: The Latin has *ánimam* (the Hebrew נפש) where the Greek has εἰς χεῖρας, 'into the hands'; the Latin is followed (rule 1). 26:12 *Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me* → *às almas dos que me atribulam* is the precedent. *ánima* here is the enemies' desire (DRB 'the will'; MS1932 *ao poder*, which is the Greek).

options.label: à vontade
options.note: DRB 'will' — the sense, not the word.

options.label: ao poder
options.note: MS1932 — the Greek's hands, not the Latin.

decisions.why: *ops* (help) + *ferre* (bring). *auxílio* is adjutórium's (glossary), so the noun takes the free *socorro*, and *ferre* keeps a verb of bringing. *O Senhor o socorra* would merge the noun into the verb. v2: the stylist heard *leve* first as the adjective 'light'; *traga* is as much *ferre* and cannot be misheard.

options.label: lhe traga auxílio
options.note: MS1932 *lhe dê auxílio*; collides with adjutórium.

decisions.why: *super* with the bed is 'on', which Portuguese says with *em*; the stylist found *sobre o leito* stiff. A preposition, not a word of sense (D2).

decisions.latin: univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus
decisions.why: The person switches to God (*versásti*), as in the Greek (ἔστρεψας); kept, with no pronoun supplied. *versáre* is to turn over and over: God has turned the sick man's bed, nursed him (MS1932's note: 'cercaste-o de todos os carinhos' — a gloss, not taken). stratum → cama (glossary row *lectus / stratum*, which names this verse). v2: the stylist found *revolvestes toda a sua cama na sua* a mouthful and proposed the Latin's own order, object first; taken (his *em sua* without the article is refused — rule 5). The two *sua* stay: the Latin has *ejus* twice. The blind reader did not know *revolvestes* and heard the sudden 'you' as confusing — the switch is the Latin's (and the Greek's) and is kept.

options.label: revolvestes
options.note: Ruling: MS1932's verb; 'turn over'. v2: after the object, as the Latin (stylist).

options.label: virastes
options.note: plainer; DRB 'turned'; heard as flipping it once. Unknown-word evidence: the blind reader listed *revolvestes*.

decisions.why: A dative of disadvantage (κακά μοι). What they say is then quoted, and it is said *about* me in the third person (*Quando moriétur*), so *de mim* is the Portuguese; DRB 'against me'. v2: the stylist: *dizer males de* is not idiomatic; *dizer mal de* (maldizer) is, and keeps both *dixérunt* and *mala*. Taken; the plural is not heard (number is grammar, D2).
*vidéret* has no object; the visit to the sick man is meant (DRB 'to see me', MS1932 *a vêr-me*). Left without an object as the Latin leaves it.

The Latin's pleonasm (*egrédi foras*, ἐξεπορεύετο ἔξω) is kept: rule 2 keeps the Latin's repetitions, and the contrast inside / outside (*ingrediebátur … egrediebátur foras*) is the verse's point — at the bedside vain talk, outside the plotting. *Saía para fora* is a pleonasm school grammar marks; the subject is named so that the line is heard as the visitor's (the Latin's person continues from 40:7). v2: the stylist named *sair para fora* the textbook redundancy; kept, because the redundancy is the Latin's and the inside/outside contrast with 40:7 rests on *foras*.

options.label: Saía porta afora
options.note: stylist; refused — *porta* is an image the Latin does not have (D2); the pleonasm he objects to is the Latin's own (*egrédi foras*).

decisions.why: in idípsum is deferred (D9; glossary row open, proposal: persons together → *juntos*, one agent or a thing → *a um só tempo*). Here one man speaks *in idípsum*; the Greek ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό begins the next verse (Rahlfs: 'together … they whispered'), but the Latin joins it to his speaking. DRB 'spoke to the same purpose': the same end as his heart's gathered iniquity and the enemies' whispering that follows. *juntos* needs a plural; *a um só tempo* would say nothing here.

options.label: no mesmo sentido
options.note: Ruling: DRB 'to the same purpose'; *in* + accusative, *idípsum* 'the very same'. Chosen over *para o mesmo fim* for the rhyme *fim / mim* at two neighbouring finals.

options.label: para o mesmo fim
options.note: DRB's reading, but its final *fim* rhymes with 40:8's *mim* (checks).

options.label: de comum acordo
options.note: reads the Greek's 'together' into his speech; explains.

options.label: do mesmo modo
options.note: stylist; refused — manner, where *in idípsum* is direction or purpose; the blind reader heard *no mesmo sentido* both ways the Latin allows (the same talk; in agreement with the others).

decisions.why: L&S: to whisper, mutter. The cognate keeps the sound; *murmurar* is murmuráre's (and *murmurar* is to grumble in Brazil); MS1932 *cochichavam* is colloquial.

The anaphora *advérsum me … advérsum me* is kept. *mihi* repeats the person a third time (κακά μοι); cogitáre → *pensar em* (row; 34:4b *cogitántes mihi mala → os que pensam em males contra mim*). With *contra mim* already said, *para mim* carries the dative. DRB drops it. v2: the stylist found *pensavam em males para mim* a limping chain of prepositions (*em … para*) and proposed *pensavam o mal para mim* (the row's preposition dropped, the plural lost). Taken in part: the ethical dative, which only repeats the person already named twice by *advérsum me*, is left unsaid, and the row's *pensar em* and the plural stay.

options.label: males
options.note: Ruling (v2): the dative left implicit under the anaphora (grammar, D2).

options.label: o mal para mim (pensavam o mal para mim)
options.note: stylist's line — would also need *em* dropped; recorded.

decisions.latin: Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
decisions.why: resúrgere → ressurgir (row open, which names 40:9). *adícere ut* is προστίθημι, 'do again': *tornar a*, as 9:39 *ut non appónat ultra* → *não torne mais a*. The question is left as open as the Latin's *numquid … non* (numquid → *acaso*, row): the enemies' taunt, or the answer the Church hears in it. *ressuscitar* is kept for resuscitáre (40:11). v2: the stylist heard *tornará a ressurgir* as a doubled 'again'. Refused: the Latin doubles it too (*adíciet ut resúrgat*), and *ressurgir* is the row's word, kept apart from *ressuscitar* two verses on. The blind reader heard the question's tone as open — the Latin's own ambiguity.

options.label: tornará a levantar-se
options.note: stylist; MS1932 *se poderá outra vez levantar*.

decisions.why: étenim → *pois* (row). Here *et* is 'even' (καὶ γάρ; DRB 'For even'): the betrayal is the climax of the list. *até* carries it.

The plural is the Latin's (ἄρτους); in Portuguese *comer o pão de alguém* is the idiom for sharing his table, and *os meus pães* is heard as loaves. Number is grammar (D2; as D29 *sangue*). Jn 13:18 quotes the verse in other words (Clementine, fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-43-13.json: *Qui manducat mecum panem, levabit contra me calcaneum suum* — singular). v2: the Latinist marked the singular minor (the Latin's number); refused for the reason above.

*supplantátio* is tripping by the sole or heel (*sub planta*); the Greek πτερνισμός is from πτέρνα 'heel', and Jn 13:18 says *calcaneum*. L&S gives only 'hypocritical deceit' for this verse — the sense, which MS1932 takes (*traição*). *Rasteira* is the heel-trip itself and, in Brazil, already the figure for a betrayal (*dar uma rasteira em alguém*), so the image and the sense stand in one word (rule 2: images stay). magnificáre → engrandecer (row); super me → *contra mim* (as *magna loqui super me*, D39). *sua* is supplied: Portuguese needs a determiner, the Latin has none. v2: the Latinist (minor) marked *a sua* as supplied; the stylist named 40:10 the worst line — *engrandecer uma rasteira* is a collocation that does not exist and a jolt of register; the blind reader heard the betrayal rightly but did not know *engrandeceu* here. Taken: *magnificáre* is said *fez grande* — the causative the Latin verb is, where the glossary's *engrandecer* (praise and boasting: 11:5, 19:6, 33:4, 34:27) does not fit a thing made great; and the possessive is dropped. *rasteira* stays: none of the three readers lost the sense, and it keeps the heel.

options.label: fez grande contra mim a rasteira

forms.supplantatio: fez grande contra mim a rasteira

options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's verb, the Latinist's article.

options.label: engrandeceu contra mim a sua rasteira

forms.supplantatio: engrandeceu contra mim a sua rasteira

options.label: fez grande contra mim a sua traição

forms.supplantatio: fez grande contra mim a sua traição

options.note: MS1932's noun (*urdiu contra mim a sua traição*); L&S's sense without the image.

decisions.why: The cognate, as the resúrgere row foresaw (*ressuscitar* kept for resuscitáre). In the psalm it is 'raise me from this bed' (MS1932's note); the Church sings it on Holy Saturday (Quad6-6: *R. Et resúscita me, et retríbuam eis* — grep), and the Latin word carries both. Safe at the *vós* imperative with the enclitic (D13).

options.label: levantai-me
options.note: DRB 'raise me up again' — closes the Latin's double sense on the sickbed.

decisions.why: velle → querer (row); 17:20 *quóniam vóluit me → porque me quis* is the precedent, heard there as 'loved me / chose me'. τεθέληκάς με. DRB 'hast had a good will for me'.

options.label: me quisestes bem
options.note: DRB's sense; the row's option at 21:9 (*lhe quer bem*).

decisions.why: The Latin has no possessive (the Greek: διὰ τὴν ἀκακίαν); DRB and MS1932 supply 'my'. Left as the Latin has it: whose innocence is plain from *a mim*, and the Church uses the verse of saints (missa Sancti/06-21, the Offertory; Hildegard's office — grep).

decisions.latin: et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum
decisions.why: confirmáre with a person as object → *firmar* (the row's proposal after 36:17 and 37:3: *confirmar* is heard as attesting). in conspéctu: the row's split — *à vista de* as a predicate, *na … presença* beside a verb of setting or worship (17:7b, 21:28b, 118:168–170); here God sets a man before him (Hebrew 'before your face'). in ætérnum → *para sempre* (D23).

options.label: diante de vós
options.note: MS1932 *diante de ti*; the row keeps *diante de* for *ante*.

decisions.latin: a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum
decisions.why: The first of three places (40:14, 89:2, 105:48); D37 rules *usque in sǽculum → para todo o sempre* and leaves the first member to the psalm. a sǽculo → *desde sempre* (row, open; 24:6, 118:52 applied). The pair echoes *sempre … sempre* as the Latin echoes *sǽculo … sǽculum*. MS1932 *por todos os séculos dos séculos* is in sǽculum sǽculi's wording (D27) and drops *a*.

options.label: desde sempre e para todo o sempre

forms.asaeculo: desde sempre e para todo o sempre

options.label: de eternidade em eternidade
options.note: DRB 'from eternity to eternity'; *eternidade* is not the Latin's word, and it drops D37's form.

options.label: de século em século
options.note: Latinist (minor): keeps the repeated noun; refused — D37 rules *para todo o sempre* for *usque in sǽculum*, and *século* here is D27's *pelos séculos dos séculos* word, heard as a hundred years when alone.

decisions.why: The close of Book I (MS1932's note: a doxology distinct from the psalm), repeated at 71:19, 88:53, 105:48 (grep). *Fiat* alone, with no subject, is the Latin's (and the Greek's γένοιτο) rendering of the Hebrew *amen*. The glossary's *Seja* is for a jussive with a subject; *Seja, seja* is not Portuguese; *Faça-se* failed the stylist twice in Ps 118. *Assim seja* is the Portuguese of the Latin *fiat* in prayer (MS1932, DRB 'So be it'); *assim* is supplied, as grammar. *Amém* is the Hebrew, not the Latin.

choices.40:2: egénus → *necessitado*, pauper → *pobre* (glossary, D38; as 34:10b *o necessitado e o pobre*). *in die mala* → *no dia mau* (DRB 'the evil day', MS1932). *liberábit eum Dóminus* → *o livrará o Senhor*, the build of 33:20.
choices.40:3: beátum fáciat → *o faça bem-aventurado* (D19; the beátus row names 40:3). consérvet → *conserve* (15:1, 36:28). tradere → *entregar* (9:35a, 26:12, 118:121). The versicle for the Pope (Preces.txt) — it reads alone. v2: the blind reader heard *à alma dos seus inimigos* vaguely and did not know *vivifique*; both kept (26:12; the vivificáre row), with *à vontade* and *lhe dê vida* as options.
choices.40:4: lectus → *leito*, dolor → *dor*, infirmitas → *enfermidade* (15:4a). *super lectum* → *sobre o leito* (MS1932).
choices.40:5: Ego dixi → *Eu disse* (38:2). *Miserére mei* → *tende piedade de mim* (formula). sanáre → *curar* (6:3, 29:3). *peccávi tibi* → *pequei contra vós* (DRB, MS1932). *Sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi* is a short responsory (Major/Minor Special, Preces — grep): *Curai a minha alma, porque pequei contra vós* reads alone.
choices.40:6: períre → *perecer* (row). The quoted question keeps its capital, as the Latin.
choices.40:7: vana loqui → *falar coisas vãs* (11:3). congregáre → *juntar* (32:7, 34:15, 38:7b); the perfect kept (MS1932's imperfect *acumulava* not taken). ingrédi here is entering a room, not walking (14:2, 37:7 *andar*): the verse sets *ingrediebátur* against 40:7b *egrediebátur foras*.
choices.40:8: The anaphora *Contra mim … contra mim* kept at the head of both colons, as the Latin.
choices.40:9: constitúere → *estabelecer* (2:6, 4:10, 8:6, 9:21, 17:44, 117:27b). iníquus → *iníquo*. Natural order: the verb first.
choices.40:10: homo pacis meæ → *o homem da minha paz*: the Hebraism kept (MS1932 explains: *da minha intimidade*); 36:37 *hómini pacífico* → *homem de paz*. speráre in → *esperar em* (D36). édere → *comer* (row).
choices.40:11: Tu autem, Dómine → *Vós, porém, Senhor* (3:4). retribúere → *retribuir* (17:21, 30:24); *eu* supplied so the first person is heard after two imperatives. Holy Saturday's responsory (Quad6-6) quotes the second colon with *Et resúscita me*.
choices.40:12: cognóvi quóniam → *conheci que* (118:75). *gaudébit … super me* is ἐπιχαρῇ ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ, the Greek of *supergaudére* (34:19, 34:24, 37:17 — read in consult/parallels/ps034.md, ps037.md), so the same Portuguese: *não se alegrará à minha custa* (also 29:2). The second *quóniam* → *porque* (DRB 'because'). v2: the Latinist asked *sobre mim* for *super me* (minor); refused — the Greek is supergaudére's (ἐπιχαρῇ ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ), and 29:2, 34:19, 34:24, 37:17 all say *à minha custa*; *se alegrar sobre mim* is not Portuguese.
choices.40:13: Me autem → *Mas a mim* (the fronted object; *mas eu* is ego autem's). suscípere → *amparar* (D19; 29:2 *suscepísti me → me amparastes*).
choices.40:14: Benedíctus Dóminus → *Bendito o Senhor* (27:6, 30:22). *Deus Israël* → *Deus de Israel*, in apposition. The same verse closes Book IV (105:48, with *et dicet omnis pópulus*) and the Benedictus opens with *Benedíctus Dóminus Deus Israël*: whoever translates them should copy this wording.
choices.40:7b: The ruling on *in idípsum* is local (D9 deferred); see decision `idipsum`. The second colon is +1 on the Latin.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm40.txt, 14 prayed verses (40:2–40:14 with 40:7b; DO writes the second 40:7 without the letter; no 40:1, the titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): 40:2 an Alleluia verse and Gradual (missa Tempora/Pent01-0a, Sancti/04-28, 07-18; office of St John Baptist de Rossi); 40:3 the versicle for the Pope (Preces.txt); 40:5 the short responsory *Sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi* (Major and Minor Special, Preces, Epi2-2, Pent02-5); 40:10 Maundy Thursday (Quad6-4 versicle and responsory, whose *ampliávit advérsum me* is another wording) and a Matins antiphon (Pent02-5); 40:11b Holy Saturday (Quad6-6); 40:13 an Offertory (missa Sancti/06-21) and Hildegard's office. Jn 13:18 fetched from the Clementine (consult/bolls-VULG-43-13.json). Not in the Diurnal Monástico parallels. The Hetzenauer print read is skipped and owed.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps040.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Formulas checked with ps038/xref.py and ps005/grep_latin.py. Rulings applied: D3 has no place (no *exaudíre*), D5 none (no *confitéri*); D19 (beátus, suscípere), D23 (in ætérnum), D36 (speráre in), D37 (usque in sǽculum), D38 (egénus kept *necessitado* beside *pobre*; no *inops* here), D39 (super me → contra mim). Latin readings kept against the Greek: 40:3 *in ánimam* (not 'hands'); 40:7b *in idípsum* joined to his speaking, not to the whispering. Tests for the readers: *entende o necessitado*, *o vivifique*, *à alma dos seus inimigos*, *lhe leve socorro*, *Revolvestes toda a sua cama*, *Ele saía para fora*, *no mesmo sentido*, *pensavam em males para mim*, *tornará a ressurgir*, *o homem da minha paz*, *a sua rasteira*, *ressuscitai-me*, *me quisestes*, *por causa da inocência*, *assim seja, assim seja*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length: 40:2 first colon +4 (*Bem-aventurado* and *necessitado*, the settled words), 40:14 second +4 (*assim seja* twice for *fiat* twice), 40:9 first +3, 40:12 second +3 (*à minha custa*, the formula), 40:7 first −4, 40:12 first −3; accepted. Rhyme 40:7b / 40:8 (*fim … mim*) mended before any reader: *no mesmo sentido*. Cadences: several oxytone finals where the Latin is paroxytone (*Senhor*, *mim*, *vós*); allowed by rule 4.

codex.py not called (Codex out of credits since Ps 37; AGENT-BRIEF step 5). All three v1 readers — Latinist, stylist, ambiguity — handed to the coordinator, to be run as fresh-context readers that see only the role prompt and the target file (prayed.vos.json / blind/prayed.vos.json).

Draft 1, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; Codex out of credits). No major; five minors in four verses. «A faithful, close rendering that keeps the Septuagintal readings (in animam inimicorum, versasti, the tenses of 40:7, supplantationem as 'rasteira', propter innocentiam without a possessive).» Pointing matches in every verse. Two taken, three refused.

The closing verses (11–14) settle into genuine prayer.» Six taken in whole or part, four refused.

outcomes.reason: In part: the redundant dative left unsaid; the row's *pensar em* and the plural kept.

outcomes.remark: *tornará a ressurgir* doubles 'again' → 'tornará a levantar-se'
outcomes.reason: The Latin doubles it too (*adíciet ut resúrgat*); *ressurgir* is the row's word, apart from 40:11's *ressuscitar*.

outcomes.remark: worst line: *engrandecer uma rasteira* does not exist, register jolt → 'fez grande contra mim a sua rasteira'
outcomes.reason: His verb taken, with the Latinist's article; *rasteira* kept.

audit.note: Draft 1, blind, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context). 18 items, 5 unknown words (vivifique, revolvestes, iníqua, engrandeceu, amparastes). Heard rightly or within the Latin's range: *o livrará o Senhor* (the one who understands), *disseram males de mim*, *Quando morrerá* (the psalmist), *juntou iniquidade para si*, *no mesmo sentido* (both readings the Latin allows), *uma palavra iníqua*, *o homem da minha paz* (my friend), *a sua rasteira* (betrayal), *eu lhes retribuirei*, *me quisestes*, *por causa da inocência* (my innocence), *me firmastes na vossa presença*.

outcomes.remark: *entende o necessitado* heard as sympathy
outcomes.reason: *acerca de* restored (the Latinist's fix).

outcomes.remark: *à alma dos seus inimigos* heard vaguely; *vivifique* unknown
outcomes.reason: The Latin's word, as 26:12; *à vontade* and *lhe dê vida* stay options; evidence noted on the vivificáre row.

outcomes.remark: sudden 'you' confusing; *revolvestes* unknown
outcomes.reason: The switch of person is the Latin's (and the Greek's); *virastes* is option 2.

outcomes.remark: subject of *se entrava* not audible
outcomes.reason: The Latin names none either; the reader heard the enemy visiting, which is the sense.

outcomes.remark: tone of the question open (taunt or hope)
outcomes.reason: The Latin's *numquid … non* leaves it open; kept on purpose.

outcomes.remark: *iníqua* unknown
outcomes.reason: iníquus → iníquo is the glossary's (kept apart from *ímpio* and *pecador*).

outcomes.remark: *engrandeceu* unclear / unknown
outcomes.reason: *fez grande*.

outcomes.remark: *amparastes* unknown
outcomes.reason: suscípere → amparar is settled (D19).

audit.note: v2 (draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json, prayed.v1.vos.json; script revise_v2.py): 40:2 *entende acerca do necessitado e do pobre*; 40:4 *lhe traga socorro no leito … toda a sua cama revolvestes*; 40:6 *disseram mal de mim*; 40:8 *pensavam em males*; 40:10 *fez grande contra mim a rasteira*. New decision `superlectum`.

Draft 2: hard pass, no rhyme flags. 40:2 first colon now +7 (24 syllables: *acerca de* restored beside the settled *Bem-aventurado* and *necessitado*) — the longest colon of the psalm, accepted for the Latinist's fix; 40:10 second −5, 40:14 second +4, 40:9 first +3, 40:12 +3/−3, 40:7 first −4, 40:8 second −3; accepted.

Gate on draft 2, read by claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context; Codex out of credits). No major; four minors, three of them repeated from v1 on unchanged words. «A faithful, close rendering that keeps the Latin's oddities.» Pointing matches in every verse. None taken; the gate is clean of majors, so draft 2 stands.

outcomes.remark: minor: *mihi* dropped; *pensar em* softens *cogitáre mala* → 'pensavam males para mim'
outcomes.reason: The dative only repeats the person the anaphora *contra mim … contra mim* already names; the v1 stylist found the full chain limping. *pensar em* is the cogitáre row's regency (34:4b, 34:20, where a stylist asked for the preposition). Draft 1's *males para mim* is option 2.

outcomes.remark: minor: *panes* plural → 'os meus pães'
outcomes.reason: As on v1: the idiom *comer o pão de alguém*; number is grammar (D2, D29).

outcomes.remark: minor: *à minha custa* for *super me* → 'sobre mim'
outcomes.reason: As on v1: the formula of supergaudére (same Greek) in 29:2, 34:19, 34:24, 37:17.

outcomes.remark: minor: *sempre* for *sǽculo … sǽculum* → 'de século em século'
outcomes.reason: As on v1: D37 and the *a sǽculo* row; his wording is option 4.

audit.note: glossary.md: evidence appended to the rows inops / pauper / egénus, in idípsum, vivificáre, resúrgere, lectus / stratum, a sǽculo, fíeri jussive, supplantáre, confirmáre, magnificáre; new rows (open): *ops, opem ferre*, *supplantátio*, *susurráre*, formula *fiat, fiat*, formula *Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum*.
